novelty.justification: The novel route is a mechanistic measurement: the claim proposes “comparing the causal factors cited in the CoT against the factors the model's internal computation actually uses, via activation attribution” to produce a per-instance mismatch signal. Searches for “chain-of-thought faithfulness activation attribution,” “mechanistic CoT unfaithfulness hidden cues,” and “instance-level CoT faithfulness internal activations” identify Turpin et al. (2023) on omitted biasing cues, FaithCoT-Bench (2025) on instance-level detection, Circuit-based Reasoning Verification (2025) on attribution-graph verification, and Post-Hoc Reasoning in Chain of Thought (2026) on causal internal evidence as the closest work, but none as described directly aligns CoT-cited input factors with causally attributed factors. This is a non-trivial operationalization and combination of established hidden-cue faithfulness tests with standard attribution patching—a natural extension that changes the unit of analysis to claim–attribution correspondence, rather than a wholly new mechanistic principle.
